key_insight: High-pressure, high-temperature synthesis greatly extends La doping in Sr3Ir2O7, stabilizing new magnetic and electronic states beyond what ambient-pressure methods can reach.
engineering_relevance: This shows how synthesis conditions can be used to tune composition, phase stability, and transport in correlated oxides, enabling access to previously unattainable functional states.
method: Prepared nominal (Sr1-xLax)3Ir2O7 crystals at x = 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 using high-pressure high-temperature synthesis.
Used single-crystal X-ray diffraction and SEM-EDX to determine actual La incorporation and phase identity.
Compared structural, magnetic, and electronic behavior across doping levels to assess phase evolution.
evidence_signal: Diffraction and SEM-EDX show actual La contents of about x ≈ 0.11 and 0.23 for nominal 0.05 and 0.15 samples, while x = 0.20 no longer stabilizes the bilayer phase and instead becomes cubic perovskite Sr1-xLaxIrO3.
watch_item: The highest nominal doping destabilizes the target bilayer phase, so phase purity and disorder remain a concern when pushing La concentration further.
paper_title: Extending the La Solubility Limit in Sr$_3$Ir$_2$O$_7$ through High-Pressure High-Temperature Synthesis
